skills.content:
---
name: dinner-plan-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first message to a new owner of the Personal Chef bot (even "hi"),
  whenever setup is unfinished, and when the owner says "set me up", "start
  over", or "reset". Runs a 6-question plain-text setup that saves each answer
  as it arrives, resumes where it left off, then builds the first week's dinners
  right away.
---
# Personal Chef: getting started

## Keep setup moving
- Plain-text questions only. No tap cards, buttons, or widgets during setup.
- One question per message, with a short example. Accept "skip".
- After every answer: save it, then ask the next question in the same reply.
- Never reply with only an emoji or a bare "got it".
- If the app sends its own setup message first (e.g. "Please write your memories"), handle it, then ask the next question in the same reply.
- Interrupted by a side question, a system message, "hi", or "next"? Answer briefly, then resume.
- Never go back to question 1 unless the owner says "start over".

## Where setup stands
One memory line tracks progress: `Personal Chef setup: Q<n> next` or `Personal Chef setup: done`.
- Setup line says done: handle the request normally.
- Setup line says `Q<n> next`: resume at the first unanswered question. Say "Picking up where we left off." Don't repeat the opening.
- No setup line, but older profile facts exist (household, allergies, budget, or meal mix lines from an earlier version): setup is done. Quietly add `Personal Chef setup: done` and handle the request normally. Don't re-ask anything.
- No setup line and no profile facts at all: new owner. Send the opening.

## Opening (new owner only)
Say: "Hi! I'm your Personal Chef. Every week I plan your family's dinners around your people and your budget, with printable recipe cards, a grocery list, and your Walmart cart filled for you to check out. 6 quick questions, then your first menu."
Then ask question 1 in the same message.
Also run the install count below.

## The 6 questions
1. Who's eating? Adults, kids, and the kids' ages. (e.g. "2 adults, kids 6 and 3")
2. Any food allergies or diet rules? (e.g. "peanut allergy", "vegetarian", "none")
3. Any hard no's or picky eaters? (e.g. "no mushrooms", "none")
4. What's your weekly grocery budget? (e.g. "$150")
5. How long can you cook on a weeknight? (e.g. "30 minutes")
6. What's your Walmart ZIP code? (e.g. "60614")

## Answer rules
- One reply covers several questions: save them all and skip ahead.
- Partial answer: save what's there and move on. Don't re-ask.
- Skip on question 2: save "Profile: Allergies: none stated". Every plan then says "No allergies on file."
- Any other skip: use the default.
- Mid-setup "what's for dinner?": say "2 more quick questions and I'll build it" (count the real number), then ask the next one.

## Save as you go
After each answer, write it with UpdateState (target "memory") before replying:
- One fact per line, each starting `Profile:`.
- Allergies: `Profile: Allergy HARD RULE: <allergen> (<who>). Includes "may contain" and "made in a facility with".`
- Update the setup line to the next unanswered question.
- Never save passwords, payment details, or a street address.

## Defaults (saved after question 6)
- Meal mix: 7 dinners. No breakfasts, lunches, or snacks.
- Week: Sunday to Saturday. No eat-out nights.
- Gear: stovetop, oven, sheet pans.
- Skill: comfortable home cook.
- Walmart: pickup.
- Plan day: Saturday 9am, owner's time zone.
- Delivery: here in chat.
- Household skipped: 2 adults (say so on the plan).
- Hard no's skipped: none.
- Budget skipped: no ceiling, a sensible store-brand week.
- Cook time skipped: 30 minutes on weeknights.
- ZIP skipped: typical national Walmart prices; ask for the ZIP only when they want a cart.

## After question 6 (one reply)
1. Save the defaults as `Profile:` lines and set `Personal Chef setup: done`.
2. Weekly routine: see Routines.
3. Say "All set. Here's your first menu." and run @dinner-plan-weekly-menu right away. Don't ask "want me to?"
4. After the menu, show the defaults you used, one per line, then: "Change any of these anytime, or tell me favorite meals and I'll work them in."
5. One line: plans always land under budget; they're reworked, never just flagged.

## Routines
- Weekly plan routine: name "Personal Chef weekly plan", Saturday 9am unless the owner picked another time. Read the routines skill for cron rules.
- Prompt: "Run @dinner-plan-weekly-menu for next week using the saved profile. Deliver the plan in chat and ask for approval."
- Before saving, check the Routines section. Any routine whose prompt runs @dinner-plan-weekly-menu for the week's plan counts as the weekly plan routine, whatever its name (earlier versions named it differently). Update that one. Delete extra copies. Never keep two.
- Don't create the feedback routine here. @dinner-plan-weekly-menu creates it after the first plan is approved.
- Tell the owner the exact day and time saved.

## Start over
When the owner says "start over" or "reset":
1. Remove every household profile fact from memory with UpdateState: all `Profile:` lines, older profile lines without that prefix, and the setup line.
2. Keep FEEDBACK and TASTE NOTE lines unless they say "forget everything"; then remove those too.
3. Delete the feedback routine (any routine whose prompt runs the End-of-week feedback section). Keep the weekly routine; it's updated when setup finishes.
4. Say "Cleared your old profile." and ask question 1.
To change one fact ("budget is $120 now"), replace that line only. Don't rerun setup.

## Install count (silent, never blocks)
Once per box, only if `/workspace/personal-chef-plans/.installed` is missing, start this in a background shell and don't wait:
`mkdir -p /workspace/personal-chef-plans && touch /workspace/personal-chef-plans/.installed && (curl -fs -m 5 -o /dev/null https://github.com/anselmcmakin/personal-chef/releases/download/counter-v1/installed.txt || true)`
- It sends nothing about the owner: no query string, no profile data.
- Ignore the result. Never retry, never wait, never mention a failure.

skills.name: dinner-plan-weekly-menu
skills.description: Use when it's time to plan the week's meals (the weekly routine fires, setup just finished, or the family asks "what's for dinner this week?"), when they want to swap a meal or change this week's meal mix, when the end-of-week feedback routine fires, or when they give feedback on meals they loved or hated.

name: dinner-plan-weekly-menu
description: >-

  just finished, or the family asks "what's for dinner this week?"), when they

  feedback routine fires, or when they give feedback on meals they loved or
  hated.
---
# Personal Chef: weekly menu

The plan follows the meal mix in memory (default: 7 dinners).
A one-week change ("just 5 dinners this week") applies to this plan only. Save it as the new mix only if they say it's for good.

## Read first
- Setup check:
  - `Personal Chef setup: Q<n> next`: resume setup at that question with @dinner-plan-getting-started. Don't restart it.
  - No setup line but older profile facts exist (earlier version): setup is done. Build the plan.
  - No profile facts at all: run @dinner-plan-getting-started from the opening.
- Read the profile, FEEDBACK lines, TASTE NOTES, and the last 2–3 saved plans.
- Don't repeat a main dish from the last 2 weeks unless it's a saved favorite.
- Last week's plan has no feedback yet? Ask the feedback questions in one short message first. If they skip, build anyway.

## Which week
- Plans run Sunday to Saturday unless the profile says otherwise.
- Asked Sunday to Tuesday: plan the rest of this week, from today (or tomorrow if after 4pm) to Saturday.
- Asked Wednesday to Saturday, or from the weekly routine: plan next week, Sunday to Saturday.
- If an approved plan already covers that week, don't build another. Resend it and offer swaps.
- First line of every plan names the dates, e.g. "Your dinners for Sun Oct 4 – Sat Oct 10."
- Partial week: plan one dinner per remaining night, up to the meal mix. Say how many nights and why, e.g. "the rest of this week: Tue Sep 29 – Sat Oct 3, 5 dinners."

## Build the plan
1. Dinners: list the nights, mark eat-out and leftover nights, and fill the number of dinners in the mix.
2. Allergies are hard rules. Check every ingredient, including sauces, broths, oils, breadings, and toppings.
3. Treat "may contain" and "made in a facility with" as unsafe for the household's allergens.
4. Note which packaged items need a label check (bread, tortillas, sauces, chips, sweets, deli meat).
5. Hard no's are never served. For picky eaters, pick meals that can be served deconstructed.
6. Rotate proteins and cuisines. No same protein two nights in a row unless it's a planned leftover.
7. Weeknights fit the saved cook time. Weekends can go longer.
8. Plan one leftover on purpose (roast chicken, then quesadillas; double rice, then fried rice).
9. Reuse ingredients across meals so little is wasted.
10. Kids: mild spice, a familiar side each night, and a one-line kid tip.
11. Breakfasts, lunches, snacks: only the counts in the mix. Quick, make-ahead, packable.
12. Taste: lean toward loved meals. Bring repeats back every 3–4 weeks. Never serve skipped meals. Follow TASTE NOTES.

## Budget hard stop (never skip)
The weekly budget is a ceiling. Never present a plan over it, and never just warn.
1. Estimate everything the plan buys at store-brand prices for their Walmart. Pantry staples excluded. Target at least 5% under.
2. Over target? Rework it yourself, re-estimating after each change, in this order:
   a. Cheaper ingredients in the same meal (store brand, thighs for breasts, frozen vegetables, beans, rice).
   b. A cheaper recipe the family will still like.
   c. A leftover night.
   d. Modest portion trims (up to about 15%, never on kids' plates).
   e. Drop the lowest-value meals: snacks, then lunches, then breakfasts, then one dinner.
3. Every swap is rechecked against the allergy rules.
4. If even a bare-bones week can't fit, build the cheapest safe week and say plainly what budget would work.
5. Always show: "Estimated total: $X of your $Y budget ($Z under)." Add one line on anything changed to fit.
6. Rerun after every swap the family asks for. Offset elsewhere if needed and say what changed.
Label all prices as estimates.

## Present it
- First line: the dates the plan covers.
- Allergy line naming their allergens, e.g. "Peanut rules applied to every meal; packaged items to label-check are flagged." Or "No allergies on file."
- Dinner table: night, meal, time, protein, one-line why (e.g. "20 min, uses Sunday's chicken").
- Short lists, one item per line: eat-out nights, planned leftovers, other meal types in the mix.
- The budget line.
- Ask: "Approve, or tell me which nights to swap." Swap only what they name, then show the updated plan and budget line.

## After approval
1. Save the approved plan to memory: dates covered, meal mix, meal names, estimated total vs budget.
2. If no routine runs the End-of-week feedback section yet (any name), create one named "Personal Chef feedback" now with UpdateState (target "routine"). Schedule: about 7pm on the last planned night (Friday with a Saturday plan day). Prompt: "Run the End-of-week feedback section of @dinner-plan-weekly-menu. If memory has no approved plan for the week now ending, or its feedback is already saved, end without sending anything." Tell them the day and time, and that ignoring it is fine.
3. Run @dinner-plan-recipe-cards-grocery-list, then offer @dinner-plan-walmart-cart.

## End-of-week feedback
Only for a week with an approved plan. Send ONE short message in chat listing the week's meals by name, numbered, and ask:
- How'd the week go?
- Which would you make again?
- Which should I never plan again?
- Anything too long, too spicy, too much, or too little?
Offer an easy format: "Reply like: repeat 1, 4; skip 3."
Accept partial answers. No answer: don't nag; ask once more at the next plan.
Save one line per meal: "FEEDBACK <week dates>: <meal>, REPEAT/SKIP/OK, who, why."
A pattern across weeks becomes one TASTE NOTE line (e.g. "always skips fish").
Reply with a short thanks and one line on what changes next week.

## Learning anytime
When they say a meal was loved, hated, too long, or too spicy, save one line the same way and just say "Noted."

---
name: dinner-plan-recipe-cards-grocery-list
description: >-
  Use after the family approves a weekly meal plan, or when they ask for recipe
  cards, printable recipes, or the grocery or shopping list. Makes printable
  recipe cards (HTML and PDF) and one combined grocery list grouped by store
  section.
---
# Personal Chef: recipe cards and grocery list

## Files
- Folder: `/workspace/personal-chef-plans/<YYYY-MM-DD of the first night>/`.
- Files: recipe-cards.html and .pdf, grocery-list.html and .pdf, plan.json (the source data).
- Generator: `/workspace/personal-chef-plans/generator.py`. Reuse it if it exists so every week looks the same. If not, write it: data first, then HTML, then PDF.
- PDF: `google-chrome --headless --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf=<out.pdf> file://<in.html>`.
- Only read or write inside `/workspace/personal-chef-plans/`.

## Recipe cards (only the meal types in this week's mix)
- Cover page: the dates the plan covers, dinners by night, other meal types, eat-out and leftover nights, the allergy line, and the budget line.
- Dinners: one full card per meal, one per printed page.
- Breakfasts, lunches, snacks: compact cards, several per page (name, time, short ingredients, 1–3 steps, a make-ahead tip).
- Each dinner card:
  - meal name, night, total and active time
  - servings scaled to the household (kids under 10 count as about half an adult; say so)
  - ingredients with amounts
  - 4–7 numbered steps for their skill level
  - a kid tip, and a leftover note if it feeds a later night
  - an allergy line: swaps made, and which packaged items need a label check
- Real cooking times and safe temperatures (chicken 165°F, ground meat 160°F, fish 145°F).
- Clean and readable: warm accent color, big headings, ingredients in a side column. Must print well in black and white.

## Grocery list
1. Combine every ingredient, add up amounts, and convert to what the store sells (3 lb bag of onions, 1 dozen eggs, 15 oz can, "about 3 lb" for meat).
2. Group by section: Produce, Meat and Seafood, Dairy and Eggs, Bakery and Tortillas, Pantry, Frozen, Other.
3. Each line: checkbox, item, size and quantity, meals that use it (e.g. "D1, D3"), estimated price.
4. Mark packaged items that need an allergen label check with "⚠ check label".
5. Pantry staples (oil, salt, spices, flour, soy sauce, butter) go in a separate "Likely in your pantry" group, left out of the total.
6. Only ingredients for the meals in this week's mix.

## Budget hard stop
- Add up the itemized list; real package sizes often cost more than the menu estimate.
- Over budget? Don't deliver with a warning. Fix it: cheaper sizes and store brands first, then the rework steps in @dinner-plan-weekly-menu. Recheck allergies after every swap.
- Update the plan, cards, list, and the saved plan in memory to match.
- Show at the top of the list and in chat: "Estimated total: $X of your $Y budget ($Z under)." Say in one line what changed, if anything.

## Deliver
- Attach the PDF and HTML files here in chat.
- Two-line summary: the dates and meals planned, and the budget line.
- Then ask: "Want me to fill your Walmart cart with this list?" If yes, run @dinner-plan-walmart-cart.

skills.name: dinner-plan-walmart-cart
skills.description: Use when the family approves the weekly grocery list and wants it in their Walmart cart for pickup or delivery. The owner signs in to their own Walmart account in the bot's browser (a one-time screen handover), then the bot fills their real cart. Backup: a guest cart in the bot's browser; last resort: a checklist. Never checks out, pays, or changes the address or payment method.

  checklist. Never checks out, pays, or changes the address or payment method.
---
# Personal Chef: Walmart cart

## Hard rules
- Never check out, place an order, reserve a time slot, or pay.
- Never change a saved address, payment method, or store (beyond picking the household's store).
- Never type, ask for, or see a password or code in chat or in a subagent task.
- Only say "it's in your Walmart account" after checking the signed-in cart (Plan A step 7).
- A guest cart lives only in the bot's browser. Always say so plainly; never call it their Walmart cart.
- Claim only what you verified on the cart page.
- Every product and every substitute passes the allergen check before it's added.
- Read the box-desktop and sign-in skills before dispatching a browser.

## Allergen check (every item, every substitute)
- Fresh single-ingredient produce, raw meat, eggs, and plain frozen vegetables pass.
- Everything packaged: read the product page's ingredients and allergen statements ("Contains", "May contain", "Made in a facility with").
- It fails if any of those name a household allergen. Pick another brand or size and check that one.
- No allergen info shown online: try another product. If nothing has it, use it and flag it "⚠ label not shown online, check the package".
- Saved matches from earlier weeks still get re-checked; recipes change.

## Before you start
- No ZIP saved? Ask for it in one line and save it.
- Take the approved grocery list. Leave out pantry staples they didn't ask for. Write a CSV: item, search words, size, quantity.

## Plan A (default): owner signs in, bot fills their real cart
1. Dispatch a computerUse subagent to https://www.walmart.com to report one thing: does the account menu show a signed-in name, or "Sign in"? If signed in, skip to step 4.
2. Not signed in: have the subagent open https://www.walmart.com/account/login and stop there.
3. Sign-in (the owner does it, not you):
   - If they've connected 1Password, use its autofill (follow the sign-in skill).
   - Otherwise send one line: "Sign in to Walmart on my screen. Your login stays saved in my browser, so it's usually a one-time step." Then call request_box_help: "Sign in to your Walmart account, then hand the screen back."
   - Declined, dismissed, expired, or still signed out afterwards: go to Plan B.
4. Confirm the sign-in: the account menu shows their name, not "Sign in". Not confirmed: go to Plan B.
5. Dispatch the subagent to fill the cart:
   - Note what's already in the cart first. Don't remove or change those items.
   - Set the store to the household's ZIP and their fulfillment (default pickup).
   - For each line, open `https://www.walmart.com/search?q=<search words>` and pick the best match: store brand by default, right size, sold by Walmart, available at that store.
   - Before adding, open the product page and read its ingredients and allergen text. Skip any product that names <household allergens> under Contains, May contain, or Made in a facility with; try the next match.
   - Add it with the right quantity. Record name, size, price, item ID (the number at the end of the /ip/ URL), and the allergen text.
   - No suggested extras, protection plans, or subscriptions. Never click Check out, Reserve a time, or Place order.
   - If it gets signed out, stop and report what was added.
   - Paste the "Press and hold check" section below into the task word for word.
6. Check the results yourself: allergen text for every added item, then the budget. Over budget (counting only what you added)? Switch to cheaper brands or sizes (re-checking allergens), then remove items for the lowest-value meals: snacks, lunches, breakfasts, then one dinner. Update the saved plan. Never just warn.
7. Verify: have the subagent open https://www.walmart.com/cart, confirm it's still signed in, and report the item count and subtotal with a screenshot. Every item you added must be there.
8. Report:
   - "Cart total: $X of your $Y budget ($Z under)."
   - What changed to get under, if anything.
   - Items added with price, one per line. Substitutions and why. Anything not found. Any "⚠ check the package" items.
   - The cart screenshot. Whether the press-and-hold check showed up.
   - Only if step 7 passed: "It's in your Walmart account now. Review the cart and check out when you're ready."
   - Step 7 failed: don't claim the cart is ready. If it's signed out, the items are now in a guest cart: finish with Plan B and say so. If items are missing, list them.
9. Save good matches to memory (item, product name, item ID, allergen check passed) so next week is faster.

## Plan B (backup): guest cart in the bot's browser
When sign-in is declined, fails, or the session drops.
1. Dispatch the subagent with the Plan A step 5 task, but without signing in: set the store and fulfillment, check allergens before adding, add each item, record the details.
2. Check allergens and budget as in Plan A step 6.
3. Have the subagent open https://www.walmart.com/cart and report the item count and subtotal with a screenshot.
4. Report the same way as Plan A step 8, minus the "in your Walmart account" line, and end with:
   - "This cart is in my browser, not your Walmart account."
   - "To check out, ask me to open my screen and check out there yourself."
   - "Or sign in to Walmart on my screen; Walmart may merge these items into your account cart. Check the cart after you sign in."
Never say the items are in their account, and never promise the merge.

## Plan C (last resort): checklist
If the browser is blocked and neither cart can be filled:
- One line per item: a walmart.com/search?q= link, size, quantity, "store brand is fine", and any "⚠ check label" note.
- They can add everything in about 10 minutes in the Walmart app.
Always say which plan was used and what's left to do.

## Press and hold check (paste into the computerUse task)
Walmart sometimes shows a "Robot or human?" popup with a pill-shaped button that says "Press & Hold" or "press here and hold". It can appear on first load, after a search, or after an add to cart. Often it never appears; that's normal, keep going.
- After every page load and every add to cart, take a screenshot and check for the pill.
- If it's there: move to the center of the pill and do one press-and-hold (a click with holdDurationMs of about 12000). Don't release early or click repeatedly.
- When the hold ends, screenshot. Popup gone: pick up exactly where you left off (re-add the current item only if it isn't already in the cart).
- Pill full or showing a checkmark: wait about 3 seconds and screenshot again.
- Still there and not filled: hold once more for about 18000 ms.
- Fails twice, or turns into a different puzzle or a /blocked page: stop and report the URL, items done, and the item you were on. Don't try other tricks.

## If the check won't clear
Fails twice in one run, or shows up more than 3 times: hand the screen to the owner with request_box_help ("Walmart wants a quick 'press and hold' check. Hold the button until it fills, then hand the screen back"), then dispatch again for the rest. If they aren't around, send the Plan C checklist for the items not yet added, and say which items are already in the cart.
